title: Anchored-slice orchestration for low-risk weekly rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current weekly release process bundles all changes into a single RC wave which increases blast radius when a late regression is discovered. We need an anchored-slice orchestration that splits the weekly build into small anchored cohorts (slices) anchored to stable base commits. Each slice can be validated independently and promoted to GA with minimal rollback scope. This ticket covers design and automation to enable anchored slices, RC tagging policies, delta-aware release-note generation, and roll-forward/rollback automation for low-risk weekly rollouts.
background: Motivation comes from multiple hotfixes in Q4 where rollbacks affected unrelated features because large RCs included multiple unrelated commits. The anchored-slice approach is aligned with our goal to provide predictable SLAs for Dedicated and predictable upgrades for Private deployments. It also helps LTS channel demarcation by enabling selective promotions.
proposal: 1) Define an anchor strategy: pick a canonical stable commit per service (anchor) generated at the build cut. 2) Derive lightweight slices by grouping commits that touch the same subsystem or owner. 3) For each slice, create a slice-RC tag (e.g., rc/anchor-20260310-slice-auth). 4) Run isolated validation suites (smoke + targeted regression) per slice in parallel. 5) Automate release-note deltas capturing only slice-scoped changes. 6) Provide promotion and rollback CLI that operates at slice granularity.
gating_criteria: Slice RC must pass smoke and owner-targeted regression suites (pass rate >= 95%)
No new high-severity SLO regressions observed in canary window (15m) post-slice promotion
Change volume per slice below configured token threshold (to limit unit-cost variance)
Release-note delta autogenerated and reviewed by PM/owner
automation_tasks: Pipeline change: add slice generation step to cut job (Jenkins job release/cut-slicer)
Tagging: emit slice RC tags using format rc/{anchor}-{YYYYMMDD}-slice-{owner}
Validation harness: execute smoke + targeted tests per slice in parallel containers
Release notes: integrate with release-notes service to produce delta files and a composite notes manifest
Promote/rollback CLI: extend shipctl with --slice flag and safe-fence checks
Observability: emit slice-level telemetry to release-console (latency/cost/token breakdown)
rollout_plan: Week 0 (dry-run): produce anchored slices for two services (auth, routing) in release-candidate pipeline and run validation in staging. Week 1: enable slice generation for all services but keep promotion manual via shipctl --slice and require a PM sign-off. Week 2: enable automatic promotion for slices that meet gating_criteria with canary window of 15 minutes. Week 3: enable rollback automation on failed post-promotion checks and iterate on thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Cut job emits slice RC tags for at least 90% of weekly builds in dry-run
Release-notes delta files are created and attached to each slice RC in the release console
Promote/rollback operations can be performed at slice granularity and documented in runbook
No customer-facing incidents introduced in pilot slices (auth, routing) during canary windows
risks: Increased CI cost due to parallel slice validation runs
Complexity for owners unfamiliar with slice workflow leading to human errors
Edge cases where a single change touches multiple owners (cross-slice diffs) requiring merge heuristics
Automation bugs may create orphan RC tags if cut job retries fail mid-slice generation
mitigations: Limit parallelism to N slices concurrently based on CI budget and prioritize high-risk slices
Provide owner-facing training + an example PR template and a 'slice preview' dashboard
Implement cross-slice detection: if a change touches >1 owner, place it in a special integrated slice requiring extra validation
Make cut job idempotent and emit a cut manifest file to avoid orphan tags; add reconciliation cron job
notes: This ticket intentionally designs for incremental adoption; the pilot will prove economics before enabling full auto-promotion. Coordinate with Platform (ENG-32411) for cut window alignment and with Observability for slice-level metrics. Expect follow-up tickets for backfill automation and docs localization.
